faculty_group: PARENTING LEAVE. (Available to UI employees listed in A-6 (a) who also meet the specific eligibility criteria as described in Section E)
Benefit-eligible employees are those who hold a board-appointed position [FSH 3080] and are employed at least half time or greater.
eligible_parent: Eligible employees are entitled to 12 weeks of job protected leave with continuation of group health insurance coverage within 12 months of the birth, adoption, or foster placement of a son or daughter.

If both parents are employees of the university and eligible for FMLA leave under Section M, each is entitled to take the same amount of parenting leave as allowed for a single employee. Only one employee is entitled to parenting leave if both parents, as employees, have not met FMLA eligibility requirements as stated in M-3.
entitlement: Eligible employees are entitled to 12 weeks of job protected leave with continuation of group health insurance coverage within 12 months of the birth, adoption, or foster placement of a son or daughter.
duration: Eligible employees are entitled to 12 weeks of job protected leave with continuation of group health insurance coverage within 12 months of the birth, adoption, or foster placement of a son or daughter.
pay_fraction: Employees can choose to use a combination of accrued paid leave or unpaid leave. Employees must first use accrued sick leave (see FSH 3710 M-2).

However, when the combination of the employee’s remaining sick leave, plus any additional accrued paid leave that may be available to the employee falls below 80 hours, then the employee may elect to use unpaid leave for parenting.
service_requirement: Employees are eligible for Parenting Leave on or after 180 days from their date of hire. Employees must also successfully complete any applicable initial probationary period or (extension thereof) to be eligible.
must_exhaust_first: Employees can choose to use a combination of accrued paid leave or unpaid leave. Employees must first use accrued sick leave (see FSH 3710 M-2).
dual_employee_rule: If both parents are employees of the university and eligible for FMLA leave under Section M, each is entitled to take the same amount of parenting leave as allowed for a single employee. Only one employee is entitled to parenting leave if both parents, as employees, have not met FMLA eligibility requirements as stated in M-3.
time_window: Eligible employees are entitled to 12 weeks of job protected leave with continuation of group health insurance coverage within 12 months of the birth, adoption, or foster placement of a son or daughter.
notice: When the need for Parenting Leave is foreseeable, an employee must request an application at least thirty (30) days in advance of the need for leave.
relationship_to_fmla: If an employee is eligible for FMLA leave under Section M, the Parenting Leave described in this section E. is intended to encompass the university’s obligation to provide Family Medical Leave under the federal Family Medical Leave Act.

Parenting Leave taken under Section E. by an employee who is also eligible for Family Medical Leave shall be counted as Family Medical Leave to the full extent of the employee’s eligibility for Family Medical Leave at the time the leave is taken.
Parenting Leave that falls outside of the requirements of the Family Medical Leave Act does not count against an employee’s Family Medical Leave entitlement.

Parenting leave is separate and distinct from medical leave taken by a birth mother related to serious health conditions associated with pregnancy and child birth and from medical leave taken by either parent to care for a child with a serious health condition.
summary_page: Parenting leave grants non-FMLA eligible employees up to 12 weeks of unpaid, job protected leave with a continuation of group health insurance coverage within 12 months of the birth, adoption, or foster placement of a son or daughter.
job_restoration: Upon return from Parenting Leave, employees will be assigned to their same or similar position with equivalent pay and status.
foster_adoption_restriction: Leave may not be used for both foster care and adoption consecutively if foster placement leads to that adoption of the son or daughter.

flags: ambiguous: rule gap: E-1.b makes Parenting Leave 'separate and distinct from medical leave taken by a birth mother' for pregnancy and childbirth, and M-1 says Parenting Leave outside the FMLA does not count against the FMLA entitlement, so the birth parent could take FMLA medical leave and then 12 weeks of Parenting Leave; S1a needs a birth-only disability leave component, and the only disability leave here is FMLA (any serious health condition), so the leave is coded concurrent with FMLA (S1) and protected weeks may be understated

notes: Reference date 2018-03-13. FSH 3710 and FSH 3520 are the July 2017 versions (captures 2018-03-28 and 2018-03-03), in force on the reference date. The two HR pages are undated summaries (© 2017, captures February 2018); FSH 3710 governs where they differ.

No employer-paid parental, maternity or childbirth leave and no modified duties or teaching relief exist in the saved sources. Pay during Parenting Leave or FMLA comes only from the employee's own sick leave (which must be used first until sick plus other accrued paid leave falls below 80 hours), annual leave (not accrued by academic-year faculty), or donated shared leave (discretionary, 4 working weeks).

Parenting Leave vs FMLA: FSH E-5 and M-1 make Parenting Leave encompass, and count as, FMLA birth/placement leave for an FMLA-eligible employee; coded concurrent (S1). E-1.b says Parenting Leave is separate and distinct from the birth mother's medical leave for pregnancy and childbirth, and M-1 that Parenting Leave outside the FMLA does not count against the FMLA entitlement; that would let a birth parent take FMLA medical leave and then Parenting Leave, but S1a requires a birth-only disability leave component and none exists here (FMLA covers any serious health condition). Flagged as a rule gap on c1.

HR Parenting Leave page describes Parenting Leave as for 'non-FMLA eligible employees' and 'up to 12 weeks'; FSH 3710 E applies to all eligible employees (and encompasses FMLA for FMLA-eligible ones) with 'entitled to 12 weeks'. Governing FSH coded (source precedence); c1 flagged conflicting_sources.

Parenting Leave eligibility requires successful completion of 'any applicable initial probationary period'. FSH 3710 does not define it; for tenure-track faculty it could be misread as the tenure probationary period. Coded as not excluding tenure-track faculty, with an ambiguous flag on c1.

Sick leave C-7.e: up to two hours a month of medical-appointment time without charge to sick leave; recorded in c3's evidence, not a separate component (time for appointments, not leave for the birth).
Calendar: no term length or kind of term stated; omitted (R8 default applies).

Chain, birth parent: FMLA (12 weeks, up to) running concurrently with Parenting Leave (12 weeks), paid first from own sick leave (c3, within c1), then shared leave if granted (c5, after sick leave), then unpaid → Extended Medical Leave for own condition (c6, discretionary, consecutive_after FMLA), all within a total absence of 12 consecutive months (leave_limits). Disability coverage (c11) unplaced, no length.

Chain, non-birth parent: FMLA (12 weeks) running concurrently with Parenting Leave (12 weeks), paid first from own sick leave (c3, within c1), then unpaid. Shared leave (c5) only for a family member's serious health condition.
